text: No controluser; DBLoom uses its own app store. Keep clear error and denial handling when the user's server connection fails.
Keep loggable login outcomes with optional success logging, written to stdout or structured log instead of syslog/PHP error_log.
Minimums become MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 10.11; detect product via Adapter/Strategy; refuse older servers with clear message.
Keep conditional format availability and Excel-CSV clarity; no TCPDF/curl dependency; PDF only if owner wants it.
Persist per-user preferences in DBLoom own store tied to user accounts; no session-only fallback or la_userconfig.
Keep deterministic 404/405 responses with escaped output; PHP route cache is irrelevant.
Keep bounded memory on import via streaming and chunking; not tied to PHP memory_limit.
Keep a capability check for privilege-table access rather than SUPER; use it to gate drop-database and admin features.
Keep translatable UI and RTL support via TS i18n, not gettext/po; language set is an open choice.
Keep constrained allowed-value validation for settings, defined in TS schema per 12-settings.md; legacy option set differs.
Keep sensible connection defaults (host, port, socket, SSL verify on, compress) in profiles; drop config.inc.php keys and control* fields.
Feature-to-table mapping becomes DBLoom own storage schema; which features exist is decided per feature elsewhere.
Keep tree grouping, separators and item limits as user settings with new defaults; drop logo-link options.
Keep rows per page, ordering, binary protection, grid editing as settings; drop PHP-specific and obsolete directives.
Keep default language, connection collation and title templates as settings; PHP charset recoding and ThemeManager dropped.
Keep clear startup error when settings or env are invalid or unreadable; no PHP include semantics.
Preferences stored per DBLoom user account in its own store; no session-only fallback tier.
Set a single preference at runtime and persist per user; drop cookie write and default-removal quirks.
Per-user allow-list of settable prefs (theme, language, hidden DBs); 2fa handled in account security.
Theme and language persist per user and apply on login; no cookie reconciliation needed.
Per-user/profile default connection collation applied on connect, via Adapter.
Per-page settings dialogs (browse, export, import, SQL) saved to user preferences; no ConfigFile classes.
Typed settings form validation with clear errors; implement with TypeScript schema validation.
Keep numeric, port, regex bound checks as schema validation in settings; drop PHP validator naming.
Test connection when saving a profile, with clear error; no auth_type/signon fields; uses Adapter.
Cap on stored per-table UI prefs (column order, hidden columns) with pruning; limit configurable.
Capped per-user SQL history, newest first; stored in DBLoom storage, max configurable.
Support deployment under a sub-path/reverse proxy via configured base URL setting.
Configurable temp/upload directory created on demand with restrictive permissions; Node tmp fallback.
Preferences persisted in DBLoom store per user as JSON with timestamp; no session fallback.
Preference pages per category (features, SQL, navigation, export, import, security); drop ConfigFile/form mechanics.
Export/import preferences as JSON with merge option; drop PHP snippet export and hardened upload via validated schema.
Persist layout and UI choices per DBLoom user in own storage instead of la_ tables.
Connection profiles carry host, port, socket, TLS options; no controluser/control_ key mapping.
Invalid settings must fail startup with clear message; PHP include/shutdown mechanics dropped.
Keep advisories for missing TLS and insecure DB connections as settings/health hints; no setup script.
Need reliable HTTPS detection behind reverse proxy via explicit setting and trusted proxy headers.
Keep trusted-proxy client IP resolution for audit/rate limiting; configure via settings, not PHP array.
Read server variables robustly under ANSI_QUOTES sql_mode; use single-quoted literals.
Server-level pages operate against the currently selected server.
Support MySQL 8.4+/MariaDB 10.11+ only; drop thresholds below those and use Strategy.
Load global status and variables; show error state if status fails.
Derived key/thread cache indicators; deprecated duplicates stripped.
Group status variables into sections with Com usage list.
Section dictionary for grouping all status variables.
Truncate long log entries for display.
Process row fields including MariaDB progress.
Distinguish static from editable variables.
Accept byte units for byte-typed variables; escape other values.
Keep name, collation, statistics, totals; drop pmadb flag; replication flags follow replication decision.
Users overview of MySQL/MariaDB accounts from grant tables; only 8.4/10.11 layouts, no legacy password column.
Parse grants into privilege lists with ALL PRIVILEGES/USAGE; use modern grant sources.
Translate auth plugin names; drop Old MySQL-4.0 authentication.
Status variable alert thresholds.
Same derived indicator formulas.
MariaDB progress computation and normalised keys.
Overview with traffic, uptime, start time.
Traffic rows with absolute and per-hour values.
Keep connection statistics; drop legacy formatting quirks ('---' columns), use consistent locale-aware formatting.
Keep useful quick links; drop query cache flush (removed in 8.x); actions via normal authenticated requests, not data-post script.
Status variable list with sections, descriptions and doc links.
Keep threshold alerts and alert filter; drop query-cache based rules, make thresholds data-driven.
Keep flush allowlist but drop QUERY CACHE (removed in MySQL 8.0, MariaDB differs); require confirmation and privilege.
Slow log analysis within monitor; owner decides feature scope. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: server monitor)
General log analysis within monitor; owner decides feature scope. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: server monitor)
Monitor log settings; if kept, restrict to allowlisted variables (legacy accepts any name). (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: server monitor)
Query analyzer in monitor executes arbitrary statements; owner decides scope, EXPLAIN-only would be safer. (owner decision 2026-10-23, feature: server monitor)
Com_* statistics with rates and percentages.
Show process list with full query option.
Keep active-only filter; implement via Adapter, not legacy SHOW/IS branching.
Keep sortable columns; allowlist columns and ASC/DESC, never concatenate user input (legacy defect).
Keep refresh preserving filters; implement as client polling/refetch, not AJAX-only route.
Keep kill thread with confirmation; check DBLoom permission, parameterised id, drop RDS special case unless needed.
Global variables list with session override and doc links.
Keep editing global variables; validate name against known variable list, require privilege and confirmation.
Re-read and show effective value after set; use parameterised query, no ANSI_QUOTES defect, escape on render.
Keep binlog list and event browsing with pagination; page size from DBLoom settings, not cfg MaxRows.
Database list with statistics and allowlisted sorting.
Keep batch drop with privilege check and confirmation; drop LegacyAdmin config storage cleanup and AllowUserDropDatabase setting.
Keep create database with collation; report unknown charset/collation as error instead of silently ignoring.
Keep account list and graceful errors; use authentication_string only, no old Password column or mysql_upgrade advice.
Keep privilege gate for user administration, based on DBLoom role plus MySQL grants.
Filter accounts by initial letter and show-all behaviour.
Keep FLUSH PRIVILEGES action when needed; hint only relevant for direct grant-table edits.
Privilege checkboxes at global, db, table, column and routine level.
Keep add user with auth plugin choice and strength meter; modern CREATE USER only, no PASSWORD() branches.
Keep change password via ALTER USER only; drop legacy version branches and direct mysql.user updates.
Edit privileges per scope via GRANT/REVOKE.
Revoke all privileges with displayed queries.
Keep delete users and optional drop of same-named database; drop configuration-storage cleanup, FLUSH not needed after DROP USER.
Keep copy user and rename; use SHOW GRANTS rather than reading grant tables directly.
Lock and unlock account supported on MySQL 8.4 and MariaDB 10.11.
Export GRANT statements for selected users.
Offer add user only to users with CREATE USER privilege.
